findings.finding: PJM's 2026/27 capacity price of $329.17/MW-day replaced 2025/26's $269.92 from 2026-06-01, so Q3 2026 is the first full quarter at the higher price (+22%). PSEG clears about 3,600 MW of nuclear in PJM (Q2 call), so the step-up is worth roughly $59/MW-day x ~3,500 MW x 92 days = ~$19m pre-tax, ~$0.03/share against a $1.22 bar. It sits inside the reaffirmed $4.28-4.40 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 Power & Other rose to $83m from $52m on higher realized prices and nuclear output, and the total beat was $0.06; the stock fell 0.46% (baseline 2026-08-04). Q3 2025 beat on higher power pricing and rose 0.99%.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is: the auction result has been public for 15 months and sits inside the company guide. If it were not priced, Q3 consensus would sit at or below last year's $1.13 rather than at $1.22 (+8%).
findings.independence: PSEG's own capacity figure is from the Q2 2026 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-4-public-service-enterprise-group-incorporated-stock/). The price confirmation is https://calpinesolutions.com/2025/07/23/.

findings.finding: NRC daily status reports put PSEG's nuclear units at or near full power through Q3, with no refuelling outage at a PSEG-operated unit. On 2026-07-15 Salem 1, Salem 2, Hope Creek and Peach Bottom 2/3 were all at 100%. On 2026-08-15 Hope Creek was at 88% (a feedwater pump out of service) and Salem was at 100%. On 2026-09-15 Hope Creek was at 98% (condenser leakage), Salem at 100%, and Peach Bottom 2 in coastdown to refuelling. This is against a Q2 capacity factor of 92.0% (93.7% YTD) and a Hope Creek forced outage from Feb to Apr 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nuclear output was cited as a driver of the Q2 2026 Power beat; the stock fell 0.46%. Output beats have not been paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Three point-in-time snapshots, not a capacity factor. Nobody aggregates NRC daily status into a quarterly output estimate for PEG. Most output is hedged, so even a strong quarter moves Power earnings by cents. If it were priced, it would show as Power estimates above Q2's run-rate, and there is no visible sign either way.
findings.independence: Other dates from the same NRC series: https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/event-status/reactor-status/2026/20260715ps and .../20260915ps. Q2 capacity factor from the company: https://s24.q4cdn.com/601515617/files/doc_downloads/2026/08/PSEG-Q2-2026-Investor-FactSheet-Final.pdf

findings.finding: Summer 2026 was extreme in PJM: an all-time peak load on 2026-07-02 (~166-168 GW), real-time prices averaging $348/MWh over July 1-3 against a $64 YTD average, and a PSE&G system peak of 10,446 MW, the highest since 2012. Utility peers that have already reported beat: AEP adj. EPS $2.23 vs $2.05 expected; FirstEnergy core $0.98 vs $0.83 a year ago, guide reaffirmed; Exelon $0.87, range narrowed to $2.85-2.91. PSE&G is largely decoupled through its CIP, and Power is mostly hedged (Q2 carried a $258m pre-tax MTM loss on forward positions), so transmission to PSEG is small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 'beat on higher power pricing' rose 0.99% (baseline 2025-11-03). The other six prints fell 0.14% to 2.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer beats landed 2026-10-27 to 10-30, after PSEG last spoke on 2026-08-04, and Q3 consensus ($1.22) has not visibly moved off where it would sit on guidance alone. Weather-to-PSEG transmission is a proxy that neither PSEG nor a counterparty has confirmed. If it were fully priced, the bar would be near $1.25+ or there would be a pre-print estimate revision, and none was found.
findings.independence: Peers: https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/american-electric-power-company-aep-q3-usd-adj-eps-223-exp-205-revenue-683bln-exp-655bln ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031296/000103129626000142/ex991-q32026newsrelease.htm ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001109357/000110935726000092/exc-20261030ex991.htm . findings.finding: The early-July 2026 storms were, per the company, 'one of the largest restoration efforts in its history': ~380,000 customers, 330+ crews, 7,000+ A/C repairs. The cost and whether it is expensed or deferred were not disclosed on the Q2 call. Any expensed portion lands as Q3 O&M. Management knew of it on 2026-08-04 and still reaffirmed guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior storm-cost surprise found in the baseline's 7 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: management included it when it reaffirmed guidance. The cost was never quantified, and NJ has a deferral precedent for major storms (Sandy: ≥85% deferred). If it were a known hit, Q3 estimates would sit below the +8% YoY that $1.22 implies.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary: storm discussed operationally, no cost treatment given (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-4-public-service-enterprise-group-incorporated-stock/). Same company source as above, so not independent.

findings.finding: Q3 is when PSEG has narrowed or raised the year before: Q3 2025 brought an 'upgraded outlook' and was the only up reaction in 7 prints (+0.99%). In 2026, H1 operating EPS of $2.41 is +9.5% on $2.20, against a guide midpoint of $4.34 that implies +7% on 2025's $4.05. Holding the midpoint needs only H2 of $1.93 (+4% on H2 2025's $1.85). The guide has been held unchanged three times while consensus ($4.37) already sits in the upper half. A narrowing to $4.34-4.40 or similar is plausible; Exelon narrowed upward on 2026-10-30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 upgraded outlook: +0.99% (baseline 2025-11-03, https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/utilities/nyse-peg/public-service-enterprise-group/news/will-strong-q3-results-and-upgraded-outlook-change-public-se). findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $4.37 already discounts an upper-half finish, so a narrowing to the top half is largely in. Only a range moving up, or a low end above $4.37, would be new. The stock trades below its 200-day (~$78.20) with 'bearish' sentiment per Earnings Whispers, which is not what a priced-in raise looks like.

findings.finding: PSE&G said it 'anticipates filing by year-end 2026 to update base rates', years ahead of its 2029 requirement. NJ legislation also removes the 50bp RTO transmission adder from January 2027 (~$40m net income a year, ~$0.08/share). Both are into Governor Sherrill's affordability agenda: a January 2026 executive order on rate freezes and bill credits, and PSE&G bills described by Jefferies as the highest in NJ. Rate-case size, ROE ask or timing given on the call could revive political-risk selling.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, when the early rate case and the adder loss were first discussed: -0.46%, followed by ~-5% drift over the following weeks against a flat S&P (Earnings Whispers).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is 14.6% off its high and Truist cut its target on 2026-10-15. Request size and timing are still unknown, and a large ask would be new information. If fully priced, the stock would not have rebounded +9% in 20 days into the print.
findings.independence: NJ executive order: https://newjersey.news12.com/2026/01/21/gov-sherrill-signs-executive-order-to-freeze-electric-rates-heres-how-it-would-work/7c8YW8imDF4YqQ45Qthd7z . Rate case and adder both from the same call summary, so they are counted here as one finding.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-06 Constellation and Google signed a 20-year deal for 890 MW of uprates at 11 PJM reactors in IL, PA and NJ; CEG rose ~12-15% that day. The NJ unit is Salem: PSEG operates it and owns 57%, and the NRC list shows PSEG planning stretch-uprate applications for Salem 1 & 2 in Q2 2027. Canary Media puts Salem's uprate at 97 MW. Whether PSEG's 57% share is contracted, and on what terms, has not been disclosed. Its first chance to speak is the Q3 call, where at Q2 it cited 'the potential to contract our nuclear output under multi-year agreements'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No PSEG nuclear-contract announcement in the baseline window. At Q2 the CEO said 'I wouldn't say there's inflections' on data-center talks, and the stock fell 0.46%.
findings.why_not_priced: PSEG has not commented since the deal, and no source ties PSEG's share to it. PEG's +9% over 20 days may partly reflect it. A PSEG-confirmed contract on its own output is not in the price, because the stock would trade nearer the $78 200-day than 14.6% off its high. The most likely outcome is no news, hence the small central size and the wide upside tail.
findings.independence: Salem 97 MW figure: https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/nuclear/constellation-google-nuclear-uprates . PSEG's own contracting language: https://s24.q4cdn.com/601515617/files/doc_downloads/2026/08/PSEG-Q2-2026-Investor-FactSheet-Final.pdf

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold 6 of 7 prints, including the $0.06 Q2 beat): shrank the reported-quarter findings. Capacity price +0.10 to +0.05, nuclear output +0.10 to +0.05, heat/peers proxy +0.20 to +0.10. p_up 52 to 50.

Lesson 6 (bar disputed: $1.22 EW vs $1.19 second aggregator; items inside the reaffirmed guide go toward 0): capped all sizes small; storm cost -0.15 to -0.05 because management reaffirmed guidance knowing of it; print_vs_bar +2.0 to +1.5.
Lesson 5 (inference, not a document): guidance-narrowing lean +0.40 to +0.30. The Google/Salem contract tail +0.30 to +0.15, because no PSEG document ties its share to the deal.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): rate case/adder -0.20 to -0.15 because it is largely priced per its own why_not_priced; positioning +0.10 to +0.05 because it cuts both ways.
